title: SiteSkin Manifest 1.0
description: Structural validity ONLY. This schema is one layer of validation, not the whole of it. Origin binding, URI-scheme allow-listing, asset provenance, duplicate ids, limit clamping and contrast correction are all enforced afterwards by the security layer and are deliberately absent here — the schema does not know the origin the manifest was served from, and duplicating a security control in a second language invites the two to drift apart silently. A document that validates against this schema has cleared the structural bar and nothing more. See SPEC.md section 1.

schemaVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR. The major is deliberately NOT pinned here: version support is a policy decision, so an unsupported major produces SS-E-VERSION-UNSUPPORTED rather than a schema failure, and this file stays valid for all of 1.x.

color.description: #RGB or #RRGGBB. An unparseable colour falls back to a browser default rather than failing, so this pattern catches the typo at lint time without making it fatal at runtime.

icon.description: Deliberately a pattern and NOT an enum. The pattern is what delivers the security property: an icon field structurally cannot carry a URL or any other resource reference. Enumerating the names here would make a typo'd icon SS-E-SCHEMA-INVALID and discard the whole manifest, which contradicts the reasoning ADR-007 gives for unknown action types. An unrecognised name degrades to a generic glyph with SS-W-ICON-UNKNOWN.

matchPattern.description: An origin-relative path pattern. Must begin with a single '/', which rules out both absolute URLs and protocol-relative '//host' references. Glob grammar is in SPEC.md section 7.1.

type.description: Deliberately NOT an enum, for the same reason as icon: ADR-007 requires an unrecognised action type to drop that one item (SS-E-ACTION-UNKNOWN) and keep the rest of the manifest, so a site experimenting with a 1.1 action does not lose its integration. An enum here would turn that into a whole-document rejection. The allow-list is enforced by the security layer.
